title: Exact functors preserve bounded below derived objects
statement: Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an exact functor between abelian categories, and let $F:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ also denote the functor between the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] induced by applying $F$ termwise to cochain complexes [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. For every $K\in D(\mathcal A)$ and every $r\in\mathbf Z$ there is an isomorphism $H^r(FK)\cong F(H^rK)$, natural in $K$. Consequently, for every $n\in\mathbf Z$, $F$ carries $D(\mathcal A)^{\ge n}$ (the $K$ with $H^r(K)=0$ for $r<n$) into $D(\mathcal B)^{\ge n}$, hence carries the bounded below derived category $D^+(\mathcal A)$ into $D^+(\mathcal B)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] (and likewise $D^-$ and $D^b$).

source.place: Lemma 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor): an exact functor carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and every complex computes RF, so RF is defined on D^+ and D; the preservation of the bounded (above, below) subcategories is stated in sites-cohomology.tex, Section 0735 (section-base-change-map), paragraph before Lemma 0736
